items.title: Agentic inequality
items.summary_raw: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01318-5 Sharp et al. investigate the implications of unequal access to AI agents and of differences in their quality and number, developing a conceptual framework to identify potential sources of inequality and suggesting a research agenda to help address the resulting societal challenge.
items.headline_fa: تحلیل نابرابری دسترسی به عوامل هوش مصنوعی
items.summary_fa: این مقاله به بررسی پیامدهای نابرابری در دسترسی به عوامل هوش مصنوعی و تفاوت‌های کیفیت و تعداد آن‌ها می‌پردازد. نویسندگان یک چارچوب مفهومی برای شناسایی منابع نابرابری و پیشنهاد یک دستور کار تحقیقاتی برای مقابله با چالش‌های اجتماعی ناشی از آن ارائه می‌دهند.
items.why_it_matters: این تحقیق به درک بهتر نابرابری‌های اجتماعی ناشی از فناوری‌های هوش مصنوعی کمک می‌کند.

items.title: BlockLock: Reproducible LLM Inference with Fixed Batch Geometry
items.summary_raw:
arXiv:2611.06977v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reproducible LLM inference requires that a request produces the same output regardless of the other requests in the batch. Existing solutions pay for this in different ways: batch-invariant kernels constrain every operator, and isolating prefill with fixed-shape decode ({our CoRun-style baseline}) gives up shared prefill compute and pads decode. items.summary_fa: مقاله جدیدی به نام BlockLock ارائه شده که به استنتاج قابل تکرار LLM کمک می‌کند. این روش با حفظ محاسبات مشترک و تنها قفل کردن مسیر عددی، کارایی را افزایش می‌دهد.
items.why_it_matters: این تحقیق می‌تواند به بهبود دقت و کارایی مدل‌های LLM کمک کند.

items.title: PSGAgent: Enhancing MLLMs' Dynamic Visual Perception for Panoptic Scene Graph Generation via Agentic Reasoning
items.summary_raw:
arXiv:2611.07408v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Panoptic Scene Graph generation (PSG) requires holistic yet fine-grained reasoning over complex relations among objects. However, current Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) applied to PSG suffer from a perception bottleneck: they function as static observers limited by fixed-resolution views. As a result, models often overlook critical relations involving small or peripheral objects and struggle to differentiate ambiguous predicates in complex scenes. To address these limitations, we propose PSGAgent, an agentic framework that enhances visual perception for PSG through a think-act-observe loop. items.headline_fa: بهبود درک بصری MLLMها برای تولید گراف صحنه پانورامیک
items.summary_fa: این مقاله به بررسی چالش‌های تولید گراف صحنه پانورامیک می‌پردازد و راهکارهایی برای بهبود درک بصری مدل‌های یادگیری ماشین ارائه می‌دهد. با استفاده از استدلال عاملی، این روش می‌تواند روابط پیچیده بین اشیاء را بهتر شناسایی کند.
items.why_it_matters: این تحقیق می‌تواند به بهبود دقت مدل‌های هوش مصنوعی در تحلیل صحنه‌های پیچیده کمک کند.

items.title: TandemBench: Benchmarking Decision Models for Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.summary_raw:
arXiv:2611.05827v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Decision models choose among predefined options in tasks such as routing and action selection. In multi-agent collaboration, a decision determines how members divide work, exchange resources, and act in parallel. We introduce TandemBench, a benchmark of 1,200 questions in multi-agent cooking scenarios where coordination choices affect goal completion. Models receive complete global information and candidate team plans, with reference answers established through execution and exact search. Models select an optimal team plan and, in paired variants that retain or remove it, judge whether better arrangements exist beyond the supplied options. items.why_it_matters: این تحقیق به بهبود مدل‌های تصمیم‌گیری در همکاری‌های چندعاملی کمک می‌کند.

items.title: The Two-Ledger Model: Transaction-Grain Cost Accounting for Multi-Agent AI Systems Across Clouds, Models, and Systems of Record
items.summary_raw:
arXiv:2611.06989v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Enterprises run business transactions through multi-agent AI systems spanning clouds, large language models (LLMs), orchestration harnesses, and systems of record. Finance receives AI cost only at settlement grain, aggregated by SKU and charge period. The business question (what did this order, claim, or case cost in AI?) cannot be answered from billing data, because providers never see enterprise transaction boundaries. The FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification (FOCUS) gives billing data one schema across providers but remains settlement-grain even as it adds AI token and requester attribution. items.summary_fa: این مقاله به بررسی چالش‌های حسابداری هزینه‌های هوش مصنوعی در تراکنش‌های تجاری می‌پردازد. با استفاده از سیستم‌های چندعاملی، نویسندگان به دنبال پاسخ به سوالات مالی در مورد هزینه‌های واقعی هستند.
items.why_it_matters: این تحقیق می‌تواند به بهبود شفافیت هزینه‌های هوش مصنوعی در کسب‌وکارها کمک کند.

items.summary_raw:
arXiv:2611.06995v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems have ushered in a new age of proof abundance, but helping humans understand these proofs requires new attention to the differences in how AI agents and humans pursue a proof-making task. items.why_it_matters: این تحقیق می‌تواند به بهبود تعامل انسان و هوش مصنوعی در فرآیندهای پیچیده کمک کند.

items.title: Trust Responsive Runtime Authorization for Agentic AI with Empirical Characterization of Policy Behavior and Parameter Sensitivity
items.summary_raw:
arXiv:2611.06996v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The policy that converts runtime estimates of an autonomous agent's condition into operational authority is rarely specified or measured. We empirically characterize the Trust Responsive Authorization Policy (TRAP), which maps an Authorization Readiness Score (ARS), a weighted combination of runtime trust, operational stability, and contextual risk, onto discrete authorization levels through an asymmetric rule: escalation requires consecutive observations above a band edge plus a margin, while a sharp drop in readiness restricts authority at once. items.why_it_matters: این مطالعه به بهبود امنیت و کارایی سیستم‌های هوش مصنوعی کمک می‌کند.

items.title: Synthesizing symbolic models of human and machine reasoning at scale
items.summary_raw:
arXiv:2611.07088v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Symbolic models offer a powerful account of cognition, but their scope has historically been limited by the need for hand-engineering and computational tractability. items.title: SAVeR$^2$: Reasoning-based Safety Alignment for Large Reasoning Models via Verifiable Rewards
items.summary_raw:
arXiv:2611.07482v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) have achieved impressive performance via explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, yet this process introduces critical safety risks. We formalize LRM safety objectives as requiring non-malicious reasoning and answers, safety consistency, and explicit intent identification. We argue that existing alignment methods suffer from poor adversarial generalization, a significant ``safety tax'' on reasoning, and unfaithful coarse-grained rewards, primarily due to their neglect of the LRM's intrinsic reasoning capabilities for safety. items.why_it_matters: این تحقیق به کاهش خطرات ایمنی در مدل‌های هوش مصنوعی کمک می‌کند.

items.title: Adapting the Process of Adaptation: Darwinian, Lamarckian, and Agent-Directed Evolution in AI
items.summary_raw:
arXiv:2611.07048v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evolution has shaped intelligence for billions of years. Artificial intelligence (AI) now raises a striking possibility: intelligence may begin to direct its own evolution. As AI agents become capable of modifying and evaluating their own behavior, how quickly could they improve, and how can that improvement remain safe? We develop a theoretical framework comparing Darwinian, Lamarckian, and agent-directed evolution following environmental change. items.why_it_matters: این تحقیق می‌تواند به درک بهتر از چگونگی بهبود هوش مصنوعی و ایمنی آن کمک کند.

items.title: Closed-Loop Agent Evaluation: Layered Measurement and Self-Calibration
items.summary_raw:
arXiv:2611.07051v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Once an agent is live, teams want to know whether it is doing its job, not just whether it throws errors. Yet most evaluation is one-off: a benchmark run, a look at traces, a single score. Its conclusions neither check themselves nor reach the agent. We propose closed-loop evaluation, an evaluation method for deployed agents. It models evaluation as performance estimation under biased raters and censored outcomes, and it requires every level's conclusion to trace back to atomic data and to be computed by versioned rules. items.why_it_matters: این روش می‌تواند به بهبود ارزیابی و عملکرد عوامل هوش مصنوعی کمک کند.

items.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Epigraph-Form Guided Exploration
items.summary_raw:
arXiv:2611.07066v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Discovering cooperative behavior in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is challenging due to the combinatorial complexity of joint state-action spaces, which hinders the emergence of coordinated behaviors from trial-and-error alone. Intrinsic rewards are often used to aid discovery, but naively combining them with team objectives can distort the learning signal, compromising task performance. items.why_it_matters: این تحقیق می‌تواند به بهبود عملکرد سیستم‌های یادگیری تقویتی در محیط‌های چندعاملی کمک کند.

items.title: PromptOps: Iterative Prompt Optimization for LLM-as-a-Judge Systems
items.summary_raw:
arXiv:2611.07123v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as automated judges for evaluating the behavior of chatbots and other AI systems. In deployment, however, their agreement with the intended human evaluation policy may degrade as user interactions and score distributions change. Existing automatic prompt optimization methods are primarily studied as one-shot procedures on static development sets and therefore provide limited guidance for maintaining LLM judges over time. items.title: EnvOpt: Automated Optimization for Agent Environments
items.summary_raw:
arXiv:2611.07372v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An LLM agent's cost and success depend on its model, its harness, and its environment. In addition to the widely studied directions of parameter tuning and harness optimization, we propose the third direction: optimization over stationary environments. Agents are often deployed in rich environments shared by many tasks, such as a company's Slack workspace or a complex collection of data sources, documents or tickets. We call these environments stationary environments. We introduce EnvOpt, a method for automated end-to-end optimization of stationary environments for any given model and harness, using real or synthetic tasks without needing any graders or reference answers. On AutomationBench, EnvOpt reduces the cost of Claude Haiku 4.5 by 72.

items.why_it_matters: این تحقیق به بهینه‌سازی عملکرد عامل‌ها در محیط‌های واقعی کمک می‌کند که می‌تواند تأثیر زیادی بر کاربردهای صنعتی داشته باشد.
